reasons: The cited Section 12.2(a)(i) is expressly captioned 'Termination by Sanofi for Convenience' and grants our party (Sanofi, the paying/licensee party) a unilateral convenience right both in its entirety and on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis, satisfying the rule's core requirement of a Customer convenience right.

RevMed (the counterparty) has no convenience right: the quoted RevMed termination triggers are condition-based (competing product under 12.2(d), failure to cure a development cessation under 12.2(e)) plus breach/insolvency, so there is no Vendor mid-term walk-away and no walk-away territory.

No early-termination fee or penalty attaches to our convenience termination, consistent with the preferred position; the failed deterministic regex is explained by the parties being named 'Sanofi'/'RevMed' rather than 'Customer'/'Vendor' and does not indicate absence of the right.

Correctly handled as a compliant finding: no redline and no counterparty comment were produced, and the residual gaps (redacted notice periods, no pro-rata cash refund in a collaboration/profit-share structure) are noted in the rationale rather than flagged, which matches the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements.
